newsitem.title: BRAZIL: FORECAST - Brazil Sept trade gap seen over $400 mln.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Brazil Sept trade gap seen over $400 mln.

text.p: Brazil's trade accounts, pressured by declining agricultural exports and rising consumer imports, should post a deficit of more than $400 million in September, economists say.

"We think the average trade deficit for the final four months of the year will be in the $500 million range," said Armando Goncalves, an economist at Brazilian bank Unibanco, which forecasts a $535 million gap for September.
A recent Reuter survey of eight Brazilian brokerages and research firms forecasts a September deficit of $422 million.

Seasonal factors, such as the winding down of Brazil's soy export period and increasing imports of consumer goods ahead of Christmas, will cause sizeable deficits in each of the remaining three months of the year, economists said.

Also pressuring trade accounts is the general heating up of the Brazilian economy over the past two months. Stronger economic growth has not only increased consumer demand but also pushed up capital goods imports, economists said.
"Capital goods imports are on the rise because industrialists are inspired by the rebound in economic activity," said Elenora Santos, an economist at the Rio de Janeiro investment bank Fonte Cindam.
The government, which released September exports of $4.115 billion last week, was expected to announce September imports and the month's trade balance in the next two weeks.

Brazil's trade outlook for 1996 as a whole has deteriorated throughout the year. While the government began the year forecasting a 1996 trade balance in equilibrium, some officials were already talking about a $1.0 billion to $1.5 billion deficit by July.

Economists, who now say Brazil will be lucky to end the year with a $2.0 billion deficit, noted that they and the government underestimated demand for consumer goods imports during the country's stagnant first half.

"We now think trade acccounts will end the year at about $3.0 billion (in deficit)," Unibanco's Goncalves said. He and other economists, however, said the country had enough dollar flows and reserves to comfortably finance the trade gap into 1997.
A Reuter year-end survey of Brazilian economists taken two weeks ago forecasts a $2.3 billion 1996 trade deficit.
Brazil's year-to-date trade gap hit $937 million in August. Average monthly deficits of about $500 million in the fourth quarter would take the year's total trade deficit to about $3.0 billion.
Brazil's trade deficit was $3.15 billion in 1995.
